title: Halo Crew Capsule
description: A cramped one-seat capsule.

title: Halo Heat Shield
description: Goes under the Halo and burns away on the way home so the capsule doesn't. It works once.

title: Canopy Recovery Pack
description: A parachute for the nose. Open it below 300 m/s or it tears.

title: Parting Ring
description: Splits a stack in two when staged.

title: Punt Hull
description: A long, flat, sealed box that floats and holds a straight course. Build it lying down.

title: Cask-2 Propellant Tank
description: Two metres of propellant.

title: Cask-4 Propellant Tank
description: Four metres of propellant.

title: Ember Lifter Engine
description: A gimballed lifter engine. It isn't efficient, but it'll get you off the pad.

title: Vesper Vacuum Engine
description: A vacuum engine for upper stages. It's nearly useless in air.

title: Zephyr Air-Breather
description: A jet that burns the air it flies through, so it only carries fuel and uses little. Its thrust fades with the air, to none in vacuum.

title: Vane Stabiliser
description: A fixed fin that keeps a rocket pointed forward while it's in the air.

title: Plank Wing
description: A plain wing to hold an aircraft up.

title: Elevon
description: A control surface that moves with the stick. Where you mount it decides whether it pitches, rolls or yaws.

title: Spire Nose Cone
description: A nose cone. It saves more drag than its mass costs.

title: Stilt Landing Leg
description: A sprung landing leg with 0.4 m of travel. Comes down with the gear.

title: Tread Roller
description: A sprung driven wheel for rovers. It rolls forward and back and grips sideways.

title: Gear Wheel
description: An undercarriage wheel with no drive. It rolls and steers on the ground.

title: Nudge Thruster Block
description: Four small monopropellant thrusters. They turn a craft, and a few can slide a landed module into place.

title: Sparrow Cockpit
description: A one-seat cockpit under a bubble canopy, for flying an aircraft.

title: Kestrel Cockpit
description: A two-seat cockpit, one behind the other, under a long canopy.

title: Short Fuselage
description: A short airframe section with fuel inside. Wings and gear mount along its length.

title: Long Fuselage
description: A long airframe section with fuel inside. Wings and gear mount along its length.

title: Tailcone
description: Tapers the back of a fuselage to a point to cut drag.

title: Swift Wing
description: A small straight wing with an aileron. For light aircraft, or a tailplane on a big one.

title: Swept Wing
description: A swept wing. It's faster than a straight wing and less forgiving.

title: Delta Wing
description: A big triangular wing with elevons. It pitches and rolls by itself and needs speed.

title: Rudder Tail
description: A vertical tail with a rudder. Mount it on top of the fuselage to yaw.

title: Merlin Propeller
description: A piston engine with a propeller on the front. Its thrust is modest and it uses very little fuel.

title: Main Gear
description: Main undercarriage with brakes. Put it just behind the centre of mass.

title: Nose Gear
description: A nose wheel that steers.

title: Tail Wheel
description: A small castoring wheel that holds up and steers a taildragger's tail.

title: Buggy Chassis
description: A four-wheel rover frame. Wheels go under its corners and a cab or cargo on top.

title: Hauler Chassis
description: A long, heavy six-wheel frame for rovers that carry loads.

title: Rover Cab
description: A closed two-seat cab that drives the rover it's on.

title: Open Seat
description: A light open seat with a steering wheel and a roll bar.

title: Scout Wheel
description: A small driven wheel for light rovers. It's quick, but it feels every stone.

title: Crawler Wheel
description: A big off-road wheel with long travel. It climbs well and carries heavy loads.

title: Cargo Rack
description: A railed platform for carrying things. It mounts on a deck.

title: Light Bar
description: A row of lamps throwing a wide beam ahead, for a rover.

title: Rung Ladder
description: A 2.4 m ladder from the ground to the hatch. Take hold on EVA with GRAB.

title: Boarding Ladder
description: A 3 m ladder over a ship's side, so someone in the water can climb aboard. GRAB it, climb, then CLIMB OUT at the top.

title: Glint Sun Panel
description: A fixed solar panel for the side of anything. It makes no power in shadow.

title: Kite Sun Wing
description: A folding solar wing that turns to face the sun. It opens when staged and tears off in thick air.

title: Hoard Battery Pack
description: Stores 200 units of charge, for the night side.

title: Spark Fuel Cell
description: Turns monopropellant into charge when the batteries run low. It needs monopropellant on the same stage.

title: Reed Whip Antenna
description: A whip aerial that reaches Terra from Luna with nothing in the way. It doesn't relay.

title: Beacon Relay Dish
description: A folding dish that reaches anywhere around Terra and relays other craft. Put a few around Terra, or one past Luna.

title: Great Dish
description: A wide folding dish that reaches across the whole system, out to Ultima. It relays other craft.

title: Glow Isotope Generator
description: A heavy nuclear generator that makes a little charge day and night. For probes too far from the sun for panels.

title: Auger Drill
description: Drills ore and water out of the ground under it. It has to be landed, still and powered.

title: Small Converter
description: Turns ore and water into propellant, and water into some monopropellant. It's slow and needs lots of charge, but a lander with one needs no base.

title: Survey Scanner
description: Maps a world's ore and ice. From a low polar orbit it covers the whole world in half an orbit.

title: Bow Section
description: The front of a hull. A mid section or stern joins behind it.

title: Mid Section
description: A plain length of hull. Add as many as you need.

title: Stern Section
description: The back of a hull, with a transom for a motor and room for a wheelhouse.

title: Skiff Hull
description: A small V-hulled boat. It handles a chop better than the punt, but tips more easily.

title: Cutter Hull
description: A long, deep hull with a keel, for open water. It carries a lot and holds a course.

title: Wheelhouse
description: A cabin with windows all round, for steering a boat out of the weather.

title: Mote Probe Core
description: Flies a craft with nobody aboard. It only works while it can reach home, directly or through a relay.

title: Outboard Motor
description: A motor for the transom. It swings to steer and only pushes while its propeller is in the water.

title: Rudder
description: A blade under the stern that steers a boat.

title: Keel
description: A deep fin under the hull that stops the boat sliding sideways and keeps it upright.

title: Skeg
description: A small weighted keel for a small boat. It stops it skidding sideways or rolling over.

title: Stabilator
description: An all-moving tailplane, strong enough to lift a heavy nose off the runway.

title: Docking Ring
description: A standard docking ring. Bring two together slowly and roughly lined up, and they latch. They can let go again.

title: Docking Ring, Small
description: A small docking ring for probes and light craft. It only mates with another small ring.

title: Tow Hitch (Ball)
description: A tow ball for the back of a rover. Back up to a trailer's coupling to hitch it.

title: Tow Hitch (Coupling)
description: A drawbar for the front of a trailer. It hitches to a rover's tow ball.

title: Winch
description: A winch with a hook, for a rover. Hook onto a craft, the ground, a tree or a rock and wind in.

title: Mooring Clamp
description: Clamps two boats side by side so they raft up into one.

title: Sloop Rig
description: A mast and mainsail for a skiff or a punt. The throttle sets how much sail is out, and it can't sail closer than about forty degrees to the wind.

title: Cutter Rig
description: A tall mast and big mainsail for a cutter. The throttle reefs it, so take sail in when it blows.

title: Broad Cask-4 Propellant Tank
description: A 2.5 m tank, with four times a Cask's propellant per metre.

title: Broad Cask-8 Propellant Tank
description: Eight metres of 2.5 m tank, for a first stage.

title: Ore Bin
description: Holds 150 units of ore (1.5 tonnes). It launches empty.

title: Broad Ore Bin
description: A 2.5 m hold for 800 units of ore (8 tonnes). It launches empty.

title: Water Tank
description: Holds 200 units of water, the easiest thing to make propellant from. It launches empty.

title: Forge Lifter Engine
description: The 2.5 m lifter engine, big enough for a moonshot.

title: Broad Parting Ring
description: A Parting Ring for 2.5 m stacks.

title: Taper
description: Joins a 2.5 m stack to a narrow one above it.

title: Shroud Half
description: One half of a Shroud's shell.

title: Shroud
description: A fairing. It keeps what rides on its ring out of the air, then splits in two when staged.

title: Hotshell
description: A Shroud for Caligo. It keeps what's inside alive under 150 times Terra's air pressure and the heat, while it stays shut.

title: Crew Member
description: A crew member on EVA, in a suit with a jetpack.

title: Flag
description: Plant it to show someone was here.

title: Pearl Pressure Sphere
description: A one-seat steel sphere with a window. It's good to about 300 m deep.

title: Abyss Sphere
description: A thick titanium sphere for one. It sinks, and it's good to the bottom of the deepest trench.

title: Nautilus Hull
description: A two-seat pressure hull with batteries in its keel. It's rated to 1.5 km.

title: Trim Tank
description: Flood it to sink and blow it to rise. It's rated as deep as the Pearl.

title: Deep Trim Tank
description: A Trim Tank rated as deep as the Nautilus.

title: Abyssal Trim Tank
description: A Trim Tank rated to seven kilometres.

title: Deep Cell
description: A battery cased for the deep. The Hoard's case fails below 200 m.

title: Abyssal Cell
description: A Deep Cell cased for the bottom of the trench.

title: Syntactic Float
description: Solid foam that floats at any depth. It keeps a heavy sphere off the bottom.

title: Screw Drive
description: An electric motor turning a ducted screw. It runs on batteries, so it works underwater.

title: Water Jet
description: Pumps water out astern, and its nozzle swings to steer. It's several times quicker than an outboard, and only pushes while the intake is wet.

title: Jet Pump
description: A small water jet for a jet ski or tender. Its nozzle steers, and it only pushes while the intake is wet.

title: Jet Ski Hull
description: A short, wide planing hull for one. Add a saddle on top and a jet pump at the back.

title: Runabout Hull
description: A decked planing hull a little bigger than the skiff, with a self-draining cockpit. It's made for a water jet.

title: Saddle
description: A seat with handlebars, for a jet ski or other small craft.

title: Dive Planes
description: Small fins that tilt with the stick to pitch a submarine up or down.

title: Lead Keel
description: A lead weight under a submarine that keeps it upright as it dives.

title: Deep Lamp
description: A sealed floodlight for the deep. Below a few hundred metres it's the only light.

title: Sonar Array
description: Shows the depth under the keel, and the way to the nearest named place in the sea, out to 2 km.

title: Rotor Head
description: A helicopter's main rotor, burning propellant. The throttle sets lift, and it needs a tail rotor to hold the heading.

title: Tail Rotor
description: A small sideways rotor for the end of a tail boom. It holds the heading and turns the craft.

title: Drone Rotor
description: A small electric rotor for drones. Use four or more on a frame.

title: Lift Fan
description: An electric fan that blows straight down to hold up and steer a platform. Hang them under the corners.

title: Bubble Cockpit
description: A two-seat helicopter cabin with a clear bubble nose.

title: Tail Boom
description: A slim boom that carries a tail rotor.

title: Landing Skids
description: A pair of skids to stand a helicopter on.

title: Drone Frame
description: A light cross frame for a drone, with a rotor on each arm and room for a core and battery.

title: Keeper Core
description: A flight computer that holds a craft still in the air or on the water, with HOLD STATION. It flies an uncrewed craft while it can reach home.

title: Balloon Envelope
description: A gas balloon that lifts about 300 kg near the ground on Terra. RISE and SINK work its ballonet.

title: Balloon Basket
description: A two-seat basket to hang under a balloon, with a battery for its pump.

title: Gas Cell
description: A big box of light gas that lifts nearly a tonne on Terra. For sky platforms and heavy airships.

title: Airship Envelope
description: A 36 m gas envelope for an airship. Hang a gondola and a propeller under it and put fins on its tail.

title: Pontoon
description: A 7 m float to hold a platform up at sea. Put four under a sea deck.

title: Side Recovery Pack
description: A parachute for the side of a stack. Two or three bring a stage down whole.

title: Heavy Recovery Pack
description: A big side parachute for 2.5 m stacks, so a spent first stage can land and fly again.

title: Side Clamp
description: Holds a booster on the side of a stack and pushes it away when staged. Put the clamp on the core, then the booster on the clamp.

title: Feed Clamp
description: A Side Clamp that feeds the booster's fuel to the core's engines, so the booster empties first.

title: Lantern Vacuum Engine
description: A 2.5 m vacuum engine for upper stages. It's nearly useless in air.

title: Broad Nose Cone
description: A nose cone for 2.5 m stacks.

title: Trio Crew Capsule
description: A three-seat capsule for 2.5 m stacks. It needs a Broad Heat Shield to come home.

title: Broad Heat Shield
description: Goes under the Trio and burns away on the way home so the capsule doesn't. It works once.

title: Grand Cask-4 Propellant Tank
description: A 3.75 m tank. A base module can stand on it, so it can lift one.

title: Grand Cask-8 Propellant Tank
description: Eight metres of 3.75 m tank, for a first stage that lifts whole bases.

title: Anvil Lifter Engine
description: The 3.75 m lifter engine, for base modules and crewed moon landers.

title: Grand Parting Ring
description: A Parting Ring for 3.75 m stacks.

title: Grand Taper
description: Joins a 3.75 m stack to a 2.5 m one above it.

title: Grand Nose Cone
description: A nose cone for 3.75 m stacks.

title: Girder
description: Two metres of lattice girder, for towers, gantries and frames.

title: Long Girder
description: Six metres of lattice girder, for tall towers and long spans.

title: Beam
description: A four-metre steel beam. It's heavier and stiffer than a girder, for taking loads.

title: Deck Plate
description: A three-metre square of deck to walk, land or build on. Join them edge to edge.

title: Junction
description: A half-metre block with a join on every face, for joining girders and beams.

title: Brace
description: A light steel strut for propping or stiffening anything.

title: Wide Bow
description: The front of a 4.5 m wide ship's hull, with a tall stem to ride over waves.

title: Wide Mid Section
description: Five metres of 4.5 m wide ship's hull. Add as many as you need.

title: Wide Stern
description: The back of a 4.5 m wide ship's hull, with a fuel tank and a transom for an inboard engine.

title: Marine Diesel
description: An inboard diesel turning a big propeller. It steers with a rudder, uses the stern's fuel tank, and charges the batteries.

title: Electric Drive
description: A quiet electric motor under the stern that runs on the batteries. It steers with a rudder.

title: Ship's Rudder
description: A big rudder for a ship with an inboard engine.

title: Ship's Battery Bank
description: Stores 4000 units of charge for a ship. That's about an hour of an electric drive at full power.

title: Schooner Rig
description: A 14 m mast with a gaff mainsail, for a ship. Put two on, fore and aft, for a schooner.

title: Square Rig
description: A 20 m mast with three square sails. It's the most sail there is, best with the wind behind.

title: Ship's Keel
description: A deep keel with four tonnes of lead, so a ship can sail close to the wind and stay upright.

title: Barge Bow
description: The front of a barge. A barge section or stern joins behind it.

title: Barge Section
description: Ten metres of flat-decked barge. The deck's strong enough to drive, park or land on.

title: Barge Stern
description: The back of a barge, with a transom for a motor and a flat end for a tug to push.

title: Towing Winch
description: A ship's winch with 60 m of heavy line, for towing a barge, a ship or a platform. It hooks onto a tow bitt if one's in reach.

title: Tow Bitt
description: Posts to make a towline fast to. A towing winch hooks here first.

title: Push Knees
description: Rubber-faced posts on a tug's bow, for pushing a barge or a ship.

title: Flight Deck
description: A 20 m floating steel deck tile. Join them into a platform: two for a helicopter or rocket, a row of eight for a plane.

title: Tailhook
description: A hook under a plane's tail that lowers with the gear and catches an arresting wire.

title: Arresting Gear
description: Three wires across a deck that stop a hooked plane in 60 m.

title: Catapult
description: A 70 m deck catapult. Taxi onto the near end at full throttle with the brakes off, and it throws the plane off at 60 m/s.

title: Headlamp
description: A small lamp throwing a beam ahead.

title: Spotlight
description: A narrow beam that reaches a long way.

title: Landing Light
description: A wide beam for setting down in the dark. Fit it facing the ground.

title: Lamp Ring
description: A ring of lamps between two 1.25 m parts, lighting the ground below.

title: Port Light
description: A red glow for the left side, so others can tell which way you're going.

title: Starboard Light
description: A green glow for the right side, so others can tell which way you're going.

title: Strobe
description: A white flash every second or so, to be seen from far off.

title: Beacon
description: A slow red flash on top, so nothing flies into you.

title: Mast Light
description: A white light on a short pole, seen all round.

title: Glow Marker
description: Isotope paint in a sealed capsule. It glows by itself, with no power, for a hundred years.

title: Glow Stake
description: A stake with an isotope lamp on top, to mark a spot. It glows for a hundred years with no power.

title: Floodlamp
description: Lights the ground below it. Fit it on a side: a lander's tank, a base or a hull.
